title: Rock Cakes
subtitle: Fruit-studded rough-textured tea cakes
excerpt: Lumpy, craggy little fruit cakes with a crisp exterior and a moist, scone-like interior, packed with currants and mixed peel. Ready in 25 minutes and best eaten warm.

recipe.sourceNotes: Rock cakes are one of the fastest and easiest British bakes. The name refers to their rough, rock-like appearance: unlike most baked goods, rock cakes are deliberately not shaped neatly. The mixture is stiffer than a cake batter but wetter than a scone dough, and is simply spooned in rough mounds onto the baking tray without being formed into neat shapes. This roughness creates the craggy, crisp-edged exterior that is the defining characteristic of a good rock cake. They were a popular economy bake during both World Wars because they used relatively little fat and sugar compared to conventional cakes. Harry Potter fans will know them from Hagrid's baking, where they are memorably described as resembling actual rocks.

recipeTools.notes: Two large flat baking trays, lined.

content.text: The mixture should be stiff enough to hold a rough shape when spooned onto the tray. If it is too wet, add a little more flour. Do not smooth the tops: the rough texture is correct and intentional. Rock cakes dry out quickly after baking so they are best eaten on the day, or stored for one day in an airtight tin.

Heat the oven to 200 C / fan 180 C / gas 6. Sift the flour and salt into a bowl. Rub in the cold butter until the mixture resembles coarse breadcrumbs. Stir in the sugar, currants, mixed peel, and mixed spice.
Beat the egg with the milk. Add to the flour mixture and stir to form a stiff, rough dough. Do not overwork.

Spoon rough mounds of the mixture onto lined baking trays, spacing them 5 cm apart. Sprinkle with demerara sugar. Bake for 13 to 15 minutes until golden. Cool on the tray for 5 minutes. Best eaten slightly warm.
